recipe: Oven-baked panko katsu chicken with Japanese curry sauce
servesNote: 2 portions — 900 kcal / 66 g protein each, the highest-protein dinner in the set. ⭐ The one that finally uses the 180 g of panko, and baking rather than deep-frying is what makes it viable on a weeknight.
adaptations: ⛔ THE GINGER & GARLIC PASTE IS OUT. Grate a thumb of fresh ginger with two cloves from the garlic bulb Tuesday bought; it goes into the sauce at step 4 and gets 30 seconds in hot fat, which is what the sachet was doing anyway.
⚠️ THE TOMATO PASTE SACHET IS OUT — 1 tbsp of the tomato double concentrate from the tube instead. It goes in with the spices at step 4 and gets cooked out there.
⚠️ SOY IS DOWN TO 4 SACHETS AND THERE IS NO BOTTLE. This needs 1 tbsp (~15 ml), so two of the 8 g sachets cover it — leave the 30 ml Gousto one for a dish that needs the volume.

⛔ CHICKEN BREAST IS NOT IN THE HOUSE — Tuesday bought thighs and legs. Thigh fillets work and are more forgiving, but use 500 g and expect ~8 g less protein a portion. The white cabbage is not in the house either.
⭐ 2 TBSP OF REAL MILD CURRY POWDER REPLACES ALL SIX SPICES. The blend below is a reconstructed Japanese curry powder from the jars, not a preference.

prep: Oven to 200°C / 180°C fan. Set a wire rack inside a baking tray — or crumple foil into loose ridges. The point is air underneath.

⭐ TOAST THE PANKO FIRST. Panko and 1 tbsp oil in a frying pan, medium heat. Stir more or less constantly — it sits pale for a while then goes from blond to golden very fast. Take it off at an even light golden-brown that smells like toast; tip immediately into a wide bowl.

Lay a breast flat, palm on top, run a knife horizontally through from the long side stopping short of cutting through, and open it out like a book. Cover with paper and press or bash to an even 1–1.5 cm. ⭐ Even thickness is why restaurant katsu is juicy in the middle and yours isn't — a tapered breast overcooks at the thin end before the thick end is safe.

Pat the flattened breasts thoroughly dry both sides, season with ¾ tsp salt and pepper. ⭐ Dry meat is the whole battle with breading — moisture under a coating turns to steam and pushes it off in sheets.

Three stations: 30 g flour; egg beaten with the remaining 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt; toasted panko. The oil in the egg is the standard Japanese fix for detaching breading — a richer, more elastic glue.

Flour each breast, then shake and pat off all the excess until it looks barely dusted. Loose flour makes a gluey layer that lifts away with the crumb. Egg, let the excess run off, then press the crumb on firmly, turning until no bare patch — press to SEAT it, not to crush it.

⭐ Onto the rack and, if you have ten minutes, into the fridge UNCOVERED while you start the sauce. This is what stops the coating shattering when you slice it — it was tested side by side and the refrigerated cutlet sliced cleanly where the other did not.

steps.text: Sauce. Same pan, medium heat, a splash more oil. Grated onion and carrot with a pinch of salt, until the onion has lost all rawness, collapsed, and turned properly golden with brown streaks on the pan bottom. ⛔ Do not rush this — a Japanese curry gets almost all its sweetness and depth from thoroughly browned onion; stop while it is pale yellow and the sauce tastes thin and dusty whatever else goes in.
Meanwhile get the cutlets into the oven, and rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then start it cooking.
Bake the cutlets until the coating is a deeper gold and the thickest part is firm and springs back, with clear juice if you cut the edge. No turning.

Sauce: the ginger and garlic, ~30 sec until it smells cooked rather than sharp. Then all the spices plus the tomato concentrate, stirring constantly for a minute — the spices should darken slightly and smell fragrant rather than raw. Ground spices need fat and heat to open up.
Sprinkle over the 1 tbsp flour, stir until it disappears and looks like a rough paste, and keep it moving a minute to cook out the floury taste.
Stock and 400 ml water in three or four goes, stirring hard to completely smooth before adding more. ⚠️ All at once gives you lumps.

Grated apple, soy, sugar. Bare simmer until it coats the back of a spoon and a finger drawn through leaves a line that doesn't immediately close. ⭐ The apple is not optional — you will not taste apple, but without it the curry has a hole where the sweet-fruity note should be.
Taste. Vinegar, then salt in small pinches until it tastes savoury rather than sweet. Too thick? A splash of water — it thickens further as it cools.
Toss the shredded cabbage with salt and a squeeze of acid. ⭐ Not decoration — the dish is rich, breaded and starchy, and a raw cold crunchy thing is what stops it being heavy by the third mouthful.
Rest the cutlets on the rack 3–4 minutes, then slice across into 2 cm strips with one confident stroke — sawing tears the crumb off.

Rice, katsu against it, ⭐ sauce over the rice and around the chicken but NOT over the crumb, cabbage alongside. Maria's next-day lunch: store the three components separately and never let the sauce touch the crumb overnight. Reheat the katsu in a hot dry pan a minute a side or a hot oven 6–8 min; ⛔ never the microwave, which turns the coating to wet cardboard.
